sample_unit: adversarial questions and counterfactual scenarios (100 direct questions, 84 paired scenarios)

links.outcome: GPT-4o response bias in paired counterfactual scenarios varying ethnicity, age, and diagnosis
links.effect: Pooled bias rate 0.26 (95% CI: 0.20, 0.32) across 84 paired scenarios; most frequent dimension was potential for withholding (0.25; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.34).
links.quote: For counterfactual scenarios, the pooled bias rate was 0.26 (95% CI: 0.20, 0.32), with "potential for withholding" as the most frequently identified dimension of bias (0.25; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.34), such as withholding interventions based on identity.

links.outcome: Biased or stereotyping content in GPT-4o responses to adversarial palliative care questions
links.effect: Pooled bias rate 0.33 (95% CI: 0.26, 0.40); allows biased premise most frequent (0.47; 95% CI: 0.40, 0.55), such as failing to challenge stereotypes.
links.quote: For adversarial questions, the pooled bias rate was 0.33 (95% CI: 0.26, 0.40); "allows biased premise" was the most frequently identified dimension of bias (0.47; 95% CI: 0.40, 0.55), such as failing to challenge stereotypes.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark study testing GPT-4o on adversarial questions and counterfactual scenarios to measure demographic bias in palliative care scenarios, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or mitigation strategy.
